tagline: Up from Delaware by the Long Woods to the Brandywine.
intro: The byway comes up out of Delaware on Kennett Pike, two lanes through wooded residential country, and runs with US 1 for about a mile past fields before turning north on Lenape Road by Longwood Gardens. From there it winds through woods and fields to the Brandywine Creek, picks up Creek Road, the old line of PA 100, and heads on toward West Chester.
The valley was a crossroads of commerce, farming, art and political thought, and many of the buildings along the way meant something to the Underground Railroad.

moments.title: Longwood Gardens
moments.text: The 1940 Pennsylvania guide traced the name to the Long Woods, where people fleeing slavery found shelter at an Underground Railroad station supported by Quakers from Kennett Square to Wilmington.

moments.title: Lenape
moments.text: Just past the railroad tracks the road crosses the Brandywine Creek on the Lenape Bridge, which takes in a parking lot on its way over.

moments.title: Strasburg Road
moments.text: Between Marshallton and West Chester, PA 162 follows the Great Minquas Path, a Native American trail dating to 1620, surveyed in 1772 and 1773 as part of the Strasburg Road.

sources.label: FHWA America's Byways, Brandywine Valley Scenic Byway
